articles.title: I got tired of babysitting five coding agents, so I built a supervisor for them
articles.excerpt: I don't use one coding agent anymore. Depending on the task, I switch between Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and a few others. The tools themselves are great. The problem is everything aroun…
articles.body: I don't use one coding agent anymore. Depending on the task, I switch between Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and a few others. The tools themselves are great. The problem is everything around them: separate sessions, separate quotas, zero shared context. And the moment one of them hits a 429 mid-task, I'm the one copy-pasting context into another tool and re-explaining the problem from scratch. I was spending real time being a human message bus between my own tools. So I built Kooyu : a local-first personal assistant that sits on top of 10+ coding harnesses — Claude Code, Codex, DeepSeek, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Cursor, ZCode, Kimi Code, Grok Build, pi — and supervises them. What the supervisor actually does Routing.
articles.author: CodeGo AI

articles.title: A Field Guide to Putting Compression at the Front of a Document Pipeline
articles.excerpt: This is a practitioner's note about one specific piece of infrastructure: making document compression a callable, predictable step at the front of an automated pipeline. No product recommendations, no…
articles.body: This is a practitioner's note about one specific piece of infrastructure: making document compression a callable, predictable step at the front of an automated pipeline. No product recommendations, no vendor names. Just the principles, the failure modes, and a framework you can apply to any implementation. Compression has three layers, not one "Make the file smaller" is a description, not a model. A working mental model has three layers. Redundancy. Repeated bytes, repeated phrases, large regions of near-identical pixels — all are candidates for more compact representation. Lossless schemes rewrite repetition without losing a single bit, which suits contracts, invoices, and source code.

articles.body: I run Jobs Every Hour , a free job search that reads open jobs from about 20,000 employers' own career pages every hour. Because every posting comes straight from the employer, I can count how many of them actually say what the job pays. Here is what the data looked like on 22 November 2026. About a third of open jobs now show a pay range Out of 645,446 open jobs , 202,628 list a salary range: roughly 31% . That is far from all, but it is no longer rare. These counts come from company career pages (Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby, Workday and similar), so they lean toward larger and tech-heavy employers rather than small local businesses.

articles.excerpt: CreditNirvana Breach Post-Mortem: What Two API Flaws Taught Us About DPDP-Compliant AI Deployment In 2026 an independent security researcher found two flaws in CreditNirvana, an India-based agentic de…
articles.body: CreditNirvana Breach Post-Mortem: What Two API Flaws Taught Us About DPDP-Compliant AI Deployment In 2026 an independent security researcher found two flaws in CreditNirvana, an India-based agentic debt-collection platform owned by the fintech company Perfios. Together they made roughly 6.6 million borrower accounts and about 315,000 recorded collection calls reachable without valid credentials. The vendor fixed both flaws on 2 June 2026, the same day CERT-In confirmed it would act. That response is worth stating plainly, because it is not the usual outcome. What follows is an attempt to separate what the research established from what it did not, and to draw out what it means for Indian firms now running AI agents over personal data.

articles.title: What we left out of our MCP server
articles.excerpt: An MCP server for a database is easy to start and hard to finish. The first version wraps a search endpoint and a SQL endpoint. Then the ideas arrive: infer the schema from the first batch, add an ups…
articles.body: An MCP server for a database is easy to start and hard to finish. The first version wraps a search endpoint and a SQL endpoint. Then the ideas arrive: infer the schema from the first batch, add an upsert, chunk files on the way in, split large uploads and resume them, add a dry run. Each one sounds reasonable, and each one turns the server into a second product with its own bugs. Infino’s MCP server, @infino-ai/mcp-server , gives an agent 15 tools: keyword, semantic, hybrid and SQL retrieval, plus the writes it needs to build and change its own tables. This post is about the decisions behind that list, most of which were about what not to build, and about what we learned when we handed the server to an agent and watched.

articles.title: Does your UTM survive the redirect? A small script to check ChatGPT Ads landing URLs
articles.excerpt: For developers and marketers in Thailand and Southeast Asia who maintain landing pages for ChatGPT Ads and want to catch broken tracking before spend begins. OpenAI's Help Center says UTM parameters o…
articles.body: For developers and marketers in Thailand and Southeast Asia who maintain landing pages for ChatGPT Ads and want to catch broken tracking before spend begins. OpenAI's Help Center says UTM parameters on your landing URLs persist on ad clicks, and that ad-review crawlers may visit landing pages with tracking parameters (those visits are not billable clicks). That makes the landing URL itself a piece of infrastructure. If a redirect strips your UTM parameters, your analytics will attribute paid visits to "direct" and you will misjudge the test. The common failure Many sites redirect: http to https, non-www to www, a trailing slash, or a language path such as /th . Some redirect rules drop the query string. The ad click then lands on a clean URL with no UTM.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 21, 1676: Danish astronomer discovers speed of light — by accident — while observing Jupiter's moon Io
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 21, 1676, the Danish astronomer Ole Rømer discovered the speed of lightwhile observing Jupiter and its moon volcanic moon Io. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 21, 1676, the Danish astronomer Ole Rømer discovered the speed of light . Before Rømer figured it out, scientists thought that light travels instantaneously, or infinitely fast. Rømer disproved this almost by accident when he was studying Jupiter's moon Io . He was trying to figure out how long it takes Io to orbit Jupiter in hopes of using it as a cosmic clock. He watched Io disappear behind Jupiter and reappear on the other side. He did this over and over every 42 hours for years. To his surprise, the timing of the eclipses was not consistent. When Earth was closest to Jupiter, the eclipses happened 11 minutes early. Likewise, when the two planets were farthest away, the eclipses were 11 minutes behind schedule.

articles.excerpt: Today, I’m talking with Hayden Field, The Verge’s senior AI reporter, about the Anthropic IPO for the third and final episode in our series about AI in real life. The AI lab behind Claude went public…
articles.body: Today, I’m talking with Hayden Field, The Verge ’s senior AI reporter, about the Anthropic IPO for the third and final episode in our series about AI in real life. The AI lab behind Claude went public on the Nasdaq last Thursday. The numbers are gigantic, but not really that important for this conversation, except to say that Anthropic has become one of the most valuable companies on the planet. The real story is what happens now — and whether Anthropic can continue to thread the needle of caring about and investing in AI safety while also being a public company beholden to shareholders. Oh, and it also continuously growing the amount of money it makes so it can keep paying its ever-increasing compute bills, which total roughly $900 billion over the coming years.

articles.title: SpaceX will retire 1st Starship upper stage ever caught by 'chopsticks,' Elon Musk says
articles.excerpt: The first Starship upper stage that SpaceX ever successfully recovered won't fly again. Rather, it will go on display as a museum piece, according to company founder and CEO Elon Musk.
articles.body: The first Starship upper stage that SpaceX ever successfully recovered won't fly again. That vehicle, known as Ship 42, launched Nov. 13 on Starship 's 15th test flight. A day later, it returned from orbit, nestling softly into the "chopstick" arms of its launch tower at SpaceX 's Starbase site in South Texas. Ship 42 made it through Flight 15 in good condition, according to SpaceX founder and CEO Elon Musk , who said it "could probably be reflown with a few weeks of refurbishment." But that's not going to happen. "In this case, because it's kind of an historic ship, we're going to, I think, not take any chances with the ship and just kind of leave it for public display, because what it's done is historic," Musk said on Wednesday (Nov. 18) during a discussion at the TomorrowX Summit .

articles.title: European-Japanese BepiColombo probe arrives in orbit around Mercury today
articles.excerpt: The BepiColombo spacecraft will finally arrive in orbit around Mercury today (Nov. 21), more than eight years after leaving its home planet.
articles.body: Mercury is about to receive a robotic visitor from Earth. The BepiColombo mission — a joint effort of the European Space Agency (ESA) and the Japanese Aerospace Exploration Agency ( JAXA ) — will arrive in orbit around Mercury today (Nov. 21), more than eight years after leaving its home planet. The big moment will come after an orbit-insertion burn, which is scheduled to begin today at 1:24 p.m. EST (1824 GMT) and last for 37 minutes. BepiColombo consists of two main spacecraft: ESA's Mercury Planetary Orbiter (MPO) and JAXA's Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter (MMO), also known as Mio.
